basic_info.name: Generic LLM chatbots as exam interpreters — the 'shadow competitor' (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Grok, DeepSeek; ChatGPT Health since Jan 2026)
basic_info.category: Free general-purpose AI assistant moonlighting as lab-test interpreter; since 2026 a first-party consumer health product (ChatGPT Health)
basic_info.country: Global; US-centric product strategy. In Brazil, arrives organically via free ChatGPT/Gemini use (7 in 10 connected Brazilians already ask AI about symptoms — Ola Doutor survey, Mar 2026)
basic_info.stage: Dominant and still compounding. ChatGPT: 800M weekly users, ~40M daily users asking health questions, >5% of ALL messages health-related. No BR-specific rollout; UK/EEA explicitly excluded from ChatGPT Health, record integrations US-only — the Brazilian 'shadow' is generic chat use, not the productized health tier
basic_info.pricing_model: Free tier IS the threat: interpretation-by-paste costs R$0 (the 'ctrl+c ctrl+v gratis' channel). Plus $20/month Plus for heavy users. ChatGPT Health included at no extra cost with consumer subscriptions. Free cannot be undercut on price — a paid app must win on value-per-real, not price
basic_info.target_user: Everyone with a lab report and a phone. Skews under-30, chronic-disease patients (81.4% in BR survey), women slightly more than men, uninsured/cost-barrier users, and 'healthcare superusers' who track 4+ metrics
basic_info.scale_metrics: US: 32% of adults used AI chatbots for health info in past year (KFF, Mar 2026) — doubled YoY (16%→32%, Rock Health 8,000-respondent survey); ~25% in the past 30 days (West Health-Gallup, n=5,660); 74% of AI users choose general-purpose ChatGPT vs 5% provider bots. 41% of health-AI users upload their own test results/doctor notes into the chatbot (=13% of the entire public). OpenAI data: ~2M messages/week about health insurance alone; 7 in 10 health conversations happen OUTSIDE clinic hours. BR (Ola Doutor, Mar 2026, n=500 connected adults): 70% used AI for symptom/disease questions in past year; 41.6% use it to understand received diagnoses; 35.4% ADMIT USING IT TO INTERPRET EXAMS/REPORTS — the direct shadow behavior this item models; 81.4% among chronic-disease patients; women 74.5% vs men 66.2%. Measured harm in BR: 30.4% over-interpreted symptoms as more serious (anxiety), 22.4% MINIMIZED signs later proven serious (delayed treatment) — error cuts both ways. Behavioral substitution: 14% of recent US AI users skipped a doctor visit (~14M Americans). This is durable behavior shift, not noise. (Counterweight: only 4% of BR health facilities and 17% of BR physicians use AI — the shadow is a patient-side phenomenon outpacing institutional adoption.)

product.core_features: Paste text or upload PDF of lab report → instant plain-language explanation, range-by-range; follow-up Q&A in natural language; differential-diagnosis discussion; 'what should I ask my doctor' lists; since Jan 2026 ChatGPT Health adds: medical-record connection (US EHR via FHIR), Apple Health/wellness app integrations (MyFitnessPal, Peloton, Function), plain-language lab explanations, appointment prep; built with 260+ physicians across 60 countries, 600k+ feedback interactions
product.signature_differentiator: Zero friction + zero cost + zero judgment + infinite patience, available at 11pm when the result lands in the app. Users rate ChatGPT answers more empathetic than physician answers (Ayers, JAMA Intern Med 2023: preferred 78.6% of the time; empathy ratings 9.8x higher) — it always has time, never dismisses, never shames. No health product can beat the generic chatbot on convenience; it can only beat it on correctness, structure, longitudinality and accountability
product.lab_data_handling: By paste (text) or PDF/image upload on free tiers; ChatGPT Health (US-only) adds FHIR record connections and Apple Health. It reads what the lab printed — it does NOT know the assay method, the local reference ranges' provenance, sex/age-specific ranges beyond generic knowledge, nor critical-value protocols. No retest cadence concept, no hardware, no trends across time unless the user manually pastes prior results each session
product.family_dependents_depth: None. No dependent profiles, no pediatric ranges, no caregiver mode, no hereditary-risk layer. A mother pastes each child's exam into an empty context with no age/sex-aware range logic — a documented failure mode (UK thyroid study: subclinical and secondary presentations missed). Wide-open gap for Dr. Exame's family pillar
product.doctor_sharing: None. The conversation dies in the chat window. No consultation brief, no structured summary a physician can trust or reuse, no closure of the loop. (46% of US AI health users say AI made them MORE confident talking to a provider — the intent exists, the artifact does not)
product.action_loop_monetization: OpenAI monetizes subscriptions and (via ChatGPT for Healthcare enterprise tier, Jan 2026: HCA, Stanford, Cedars-Sinai, MSK, AdventHealth) hospital contracts — never a per-interpretation fee and never a lab/supplement/telehealth marketplace. For the patient, the action loop ends at 'see a doctor' or self-directed Google searches; 81% of AI users take SOME action after querying (search more, try a behavior, consult a provider), but nothing is orchestrated and nobody monetizes the patient-side loop

technology.ai_approach: General-purpose frontier LLMs (GPT-4o/GPT-5.x, Gemini 2.5, Grok, Copilot, DeepSeek) answering off-the-shelf, with safety disclaimers. No deterministic range-checking engine, no structured extraction, no human-in-the-loop review, no version pinning — the model that answered yesterday may behave differently today. Lab interpretation is an UNINTENDED use case of a general assistant; that is both its charm and its danger
technology.data_inputs: Whatever the user pastes: typed values, PDF text, photos of reports; ChatGPT Health (US): EHR records via FHIR, Apple Health, wellness apps. No analyzer flags, no LIS integration, no units metadata guarantee — unit confusion (mg/dL vs mmol/L) is the classic silent killer
technology.data_interoperability: Ingestion: universal by design (anything text-like). Exhaustion: none — no export, no FHIR out, no WhatsApp, no connection to the physician. The shadow absorbs data and returns prose; the patient's history accumulates nowhere. Dr. Exame's compound moat (PDF + RNDS/REL-ready + doctor portal + WhatsApp retention) is exactly the surface the shadow refuses to build
technology.platform: Chat web/mobile apps (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot); ChatGPT Health inside the consumer ChatGPT app (US); API for enterprises

ux.onboarding: None — the user already has the app installed. Time-to-value is the length of a paste. This is the bar every dedicated product is measured against silently
ux.data_visualization: Prose. Occasionally markdown tables. No trend charts, no reference-band visualization, no severity flags, no scores — the user reads paragraphs and self-assesses. One paste = one snapshot; the second exam arrives with zero memory of the first unless manually re-pasted
ux.engagement_channel: Habit loop of an assistant the user already opens daily for work/study — health questions piggyback on an existing retention channel. But there are NO health-specific mechanics: no streaks, no nudges, no reminders to retest, no push when a new result lands. Session-scoped amnesia: no continuity, no longitudinal story, no exam-based re-engagement

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: The evidence base says: patchy and model-dependent. Accuracy on lab interpretation: ChatGPT-3.5 median 2/5 ('absence of data analysis') on basic biochemistry panels vs Copilot 5/5 (Kaftan, Sci Rep 2024); ChatGPT 33.3% / Bard 20.0% correct on thyroid-function cases, missing subclinical disease, and only ~2/3 of patient-posed answers rated SAFE (Stevenson, Ann Clin Biochem 2024). Newer models look better on simple flagging (GPT-5 93% top-1 concordance on CBC with clinical context, JMIR 2026) but: hallucinations persist at low rates even in top models (GPT-4o 1%, Gemini-2.5 4%, Grok-3 11.5% on tumor markers, Clin Chim Acta 2026); accuracy COLLAPSES without clinical context (93%→79% GPT-5 when suspicion removed — exactly the ablated state a patient's paste is in); error structure is asymmetric toward FALSE REASSURANCE (mixed-disorder sensitivity 0.63 vs 0.96 for ICU physicians; 16.7% of complex cases called 'normal'; harm-weighted errors significantly higher — Gulen, Sci Rep 2026); independent eval of ChatGPT Health found 52% UNDERTRIAGE of gold-standard emergencies, 35% overtriage, anchoring bias OR 11.7 when social context minimized symptoms, inconsistent suicide-crisis safeguards (Ramaswamy et al., Mount Sinai, Nature Medicine, Feb 2026) vs OpenAI's internal claims of 98.7%+ on healthcare tests. Manufacturer benchmarks systematically exceed independent results. BR survey corroborates bidirectional harm: 30.4% over-alarm, 22.4% dangerous minimization (Ola Doutor 2026). No published methodology for any health claim a patient actually relies on; the free tier has no clinical board and disclaimers only; ChatGPT Health cites physician co-design (260+ physicians, 60 countries, 600k+ feedback interactions) but UK/EEA exclusion shows even OpenAI treats regulated markets as unresolved
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Deliberately outside medical-device framing: wellness/informational positioning, 'not medical advice' disclaimers. ChatGPT Health excludes UK/EEA/Switzerland — regulatory-avoidance geography, showing ANVISA RDC 657/2022 SaMD rules are a real moat OpenAI has NOT crossed (no BR launch of the health tier). Health chats encrypted/isolated, not used for training (claimed); but pasting results into the generic free tier sits outside HIPAA/LGPD health-data guarantees entirely (77% of US public concerned about exactly this). Free chatbots cannot be blocked and will not be — the threat must be competed with, not regulated away
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What the shadow CANNOT do (Dr. Exame opportunities): (1) Deterministic correctness — code-based range checking with lab-specific/sex/age-aware reference intervals beats probabilistic recall of ranges; the shadow hallucinates values and ranges at 1-11.5% rates, and BR users already report both over-alarm (30.4%) and dangerous minimization (22.4%). (2) Context persistence — it scores 93% WITH clinical context and ~75-79% without; the patient's paste is always context-free. A product holding the full history + profile is structurally positioned where models are proven weakest. (3) Longitudinal trends across exams (it has amnesia). (4) Family/dependents/pediatric ranges (it has none). (5) False-reassurance asymmetry — its most dangerous documented error mode (52% undertriage in independent ChatGPT Health eval); deterministic flagging of critical values is a life-safety differentiator, not a feature parity item. (6) Closure of loop: consultation brief → doctor → questions → plan (conversation dies in the chat). (7) Language gap: LLM reasoning degrades measurably in non-English prompts (translation-controlled study, J Clin Med 2026) — Portuguese users get the WORST version of the shadow; a PT-native, BR-lab-calibrated engine can be locally better. (8) Accountability: LGPD-compliant, auditable, versioned analysis vs anonymous free chat (52.8% of BR users already distrust how these platforms store health data). The industry playbook that works against the shadow (per clinician-tool analysis of the OpenAI stack): local guideline/parameter specificity, real regulatory status as a trust signal, and daily workflow touchpoints beyond chat — structure, not scale, is what a general model cannot replicate. What WORKS that should be copied (inspiration, not imitation): zero-friction paste/upload and instant answer; always-available, shame-free, empathetic tone (11pm answers are 7 in 10 of health chats); plain-language explanations patients love; appointment-prep questions; the 'superuser' instinct to bring AI-prepared data INTO the visit (46% feel more confident) — Dr. Exame should BE the artifact the patient brings to the doctor
trust_gaps.relevance: High — this is not a competitor feature list but the ambient behavior the product lives inside. Every pricing, positioning and UX decision competes with R$0 + instant + empathetic. The strategy it dictates: do not fight free interpretation head-on; be irrefutably better at correctness (deterministic ranges), context (history, family, trends) and closure (doctor loop), then price the WORK (tracking, brief, trends, safety), not the first interpretation — which the market has decided is free
